- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% downward correction.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% downward bias to reflect mean reversion.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days); if sentiment swings sharply, apply a 0.5–1.0% adjustment to forecast based on sentiment direction.
